newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ property mkt not affected by election - REINZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ property mkt not affected by election - REINZ.

text.p: Political uncertainty associated with New Zealand's first MMP election is having little effect on the property market, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Thursday.

It quoted Real Estate Institute of New Zealand president Colin Brown as saying while some people were deferring property decisions until after the election, the market was faring better now than it had done in the lead-up to previous elections.
"You'd expect that with an MMP election things would be flaky (but) the election this year doesn't seem to have impacted on property as in other years," Brown said.
What would happen after the election, however, was anyone's guess, he said.
"Besides National and Labour, there is not a lot of manifesto policy about housing from the other parties.
"They are all concerned about housing the lower income groups but that doesn't necessarily impact on the real estate business."
Brown said the economy was in quite good shape and interest rates seemed stable.
Although rates were high in terms of other countries like Australia, they were low compared with 10 years ago.
Institutions had a lot of money available for lending and the strong competition between them meant it was possible to get a mortgage below 10 percent with a bit of shopping around.
He said rates were likely to come down further if the Reserve Bank widened its inflation band.
"Artificially restraining an economy never seems to have worked. A little bit of flexibility could be to everyone's benefit."
